text.p: Lithuanian acetate yarn producer Dirbtinis Pluoshtas said on Wednesday that its sales in the first five months of the year rose to 111.5 million litas from 86.96 million litas in the same period of 1996.

But a company spokeswoman said it expected sales to go down in July and August as its partners slow down production or halt work for routine repairs during the summer period, she said. The company exports around 80 percent of its product.
"Sales in May edged up to 23.9 million litas compared to 22.6 million litas a month before," Benjamina Jakavichiene, financial advisor to the director general, told Reuters.
The company's 1996 sales were 204.85 million litas and it had 1996 net profit of 4.09 million litas and 3.47 million litas profit in the first four months of this year.
"We are operating at full capcity at the moment," Jakavichiene said.
The company is continuing to upgrade its production lines which should improve the range of its products, she said.
The works are expected to be finished in around eight weeks, Jakavichiene added.
The 16 percent state-run company is on the A group of the Vilnius bourse.
